question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution mentions oath or affirmation by the Governor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 159**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The oath or affirmation to be taken by the Governor is mentioned in **Article 159** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This article outlines the procedure for the appointment of the Governor and the oath that he or she must take upon assuming office.
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Governor holds office for a term of five years but can be removed from office by the President if he or she resigns,
 
 
• is impeached by the state legislature, or is removed by the President on the advice of the Union Cabinet.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 156: Governor's Term of Office
 
 
• The Governor holds office for a term of five years from the date he or she enters upon his or her office.
 
• The Governor can be removed from office by the President of India:
 
• If he or she resigns.
 
• If he or she is impeached by the state legislature.
 
• If he or she is removed by the President on the advice of the Union Cabinet.
 
 
 
• Article 161: Governor's Powers
 
 
• The Governor exercises executive powers in the state.
 
• This includes:
 
 
• Appointing and removing ministers.
 
• Issuing ordinances.
 
• Granting pardons, reprieves, and remissions of punishment.
